title: Sections with support: derived adjunction and fiber formula
statement:
In the situation of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-sheaves], let
$R\underline\Gamma_Z\colon\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to\D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ be the
right derived functor of $\underline\Gamma_Z$, computed on K-injective
complexes.

1. $R\underline\Gamma_Z$ is right adjoint to
   $i_*\colon\D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, and for
   $A\in\D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, $K\in\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$
   $$
   R\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*A,K)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(A,R\underline\Gamma_ZK).
   $$
2. For an injective $\Lambda_X$-module $I$, the unit $I\to j_*j^*I$ is surjective.
3. There is a distinguished triangle, natural in $K$,
   $$
   i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K\longrightarrow i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK[1]
   $$
   in $\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, whose second arrow is the unit of $j^*\dashv Rj_*$.
   Consequently
   $$
   R\underline\Gamma_ZK\simeq i^*\fib\bigl(K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K\bigr)\quad\text{in }\D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda).
   $$

proof.text: Finite type over the field makes X locally Noetherian by LocallyOfFiniteType.isLocallyNoetherian, and quasi-compactness of its structure map makes X compact. Thus X is Noetherian and the open immersion j is quasi-compact. Complementing the given equality gives range(i)=range(j)^c.

Take the additive structure, exactness of i_*, and sheaf adjunction i_* ⊣ H from det-lem-formal-closed-support-sheaves. Construct the Hom-complex isomorphism degreewise by the additive Hom adjunction. Naturality on the right intertwines the target differential; naturality on the left intertwines the source differential, and additivity respects its signed term. This proves the specified component formula. Inside the conclusion, derive the local colimit-preservation instance from this same quantified adjunction using Adjunction.leftAdjoint_preservesColimits; hence the exact derived adjunction elaborates without a new assumption.

Apply closedSupport_injective_unit_epi from the broader support-adjunction node. Both supportPullback and upperStar are left adjoints to the very same lowerStar. The uniqueness isomorphism of left adjoints intertwines their units, so epimorphy transfers across its image under lowerStar.

Use the counit/unit localization triangle now explicitly stated by closedSupport_triangle in the broader node. Uniqueness of right adjoints compares RH with RclosedSupport because both are right adjoints to exact i_*; uniqueness of left adjoints compares the two open derived pullbacks. Whisker these isomorphisms and conjugate the connecting transformation. Their counit and unit identities give the first two triangle squares. The third square follows by cancellation of an isomorphism and its inverse. Invariance of distinguished triangles under isomorphism proves the desired natural triangle with exactly the specified arrows.

Apply closedSupport_fiber from the broader support-adjunction node. Uniqueness of the derived right adjoint compares its left-hand side with RH(K), and uniqueness of derived left adjoints compares its closed pullback with i^*. For the remaining difference, the uniqueness isomorphism between the two sheaf-level open pullbacks intertwines their units. Applying it termwise yields an isomorphism of arrows from I, hence an isomorphism of their actual mapping cones. Shift by -1, apply Q and then i^*, and compose these four isomorphisms. This gives precisely the required cone of the specified open unit for every K-injective representative.

split_report.summary: Rechecked the earlier sandbox and reused the broader existing support theorem only for its explicit adjunction and injective-surjectivity clauses. Proved quasi-compactness from the standing finite-type hypotheses, then constructed the natural triangle on injective-term K-injective resolutions and checked that its middle arrow is the derived adjunction unit. No statement change and no new nodes. Independent second reading made the homotopy equation explicit and supplied the rotation, triangle comparison and existing two-isomorphisms lemma for the fiber identification.
split_report.blueprint: Step 1 verifies inherited geometric hypotheses; step 2 realizes clauses (1) and (2) through the broader node explicitly cited in the unit; steps 3--5 realize clause (3) by the original injective-resolution, short-exact-sequence and exact i^* route.

tool_uses.why: The unit explicitly cites this all-coefficient support adjunction as its tool. Clauses (2)--(3) give derived adjunction, global RHom and injective-unit surjectivity; no new node is needed for those already-stated facts.
Its descending-chain condition for finite-type affine charts supplies the elementary compactness argument; this support unit does not prove Hilbert basis/Noetherianity.
Generic ringed-site module categories are Grothendieck, needed to apply unbounded K-injective existence.
Generic Grothendieck-category injective-term K-injective resolutions for unbounded complexes, not a support theorem.
General exact-left-adjoint criterion applies to both j_! and j^*, needed to identify the derived unit on resolutions.
General functorial triangle of a short exact sequence of complexes, needed after the support sequence has been constructed.
Generic passage of exact additive functors to derived categories, used for exact i_* and i^*.
Generic adjunction on homotopy categories including its specified unit, needed to check which triangle arrow is the derived unit.
General homotopy-to-derived Hom bijection, needed to verify the unit and descend naturality.

Generic open–closed operations for modules over the actual sheaf of rings: step 3 uses exact j_! left adjoint to exact j^*, and step 5 uses the counit i^*i_* ≅ id. This is the ring-sheaf form of the unit’s stipulated open–closed input, not a replacement localization proof.
